cf.title: ALTER COLUMN SET EXPRESSION on partitions not work in case of dependencies

input.subject: ALTER COLUMN SET EXPRESSION on partitions not work in case of constraint dependencies

verdict_reasoning: The bug is real and no surviving objection questions the goal. The remaining points are fixable design points at level 2: standards-compat-1 (the back-branch error also rejects an ONLY case that works today), maintenance-fit-2 (set expression gets its own path for dependent constraints) and replication-ondisk-1 (no guidance for partitions already affected). A committer who knows the ALTER TABLE rebuild code has to decide the scope of the back-branch error.

brief.title: Fix alter column set expression on partitions with dependent objects
brief.problem: Running alter table ... alter column ... set expression directly on a partition silently drops inherited CHECK and NOT NULL constraints on the generated column without recreating them. With alter table only on a partitioned parent, an index on the column plus a foreign key leads to a "could not read blocks" error. The bug affects users of generated columns on partitioned or inherited tables since PG17.
brief.proposed_design: There are two alternative patches. The bugfix patch, meant for back branches, errors out when set expression runs directly on a child table or with only and the column has dependent indexes or constraints. The second patch, a proof of concept, lets set expression on a partition succeed when the column has only NOT NULL, CHECK or FOREIGN KEY dependents, and re-validates them in phase 3 without rebuilding them.
user_visible_surface: New error when alter table ... alter column ... set expression runs on a child table whose generated column has dependent indexes or constraints.
New error when alter table only ... alter column ... set expression runs and the generated column has dependent objects.
With the second patch, set expression on a partition re-validates CHECK, NOT NULL and FOREIGN KEY constraints without dropping and recreating them.
author_claims: The bug has existed since PG17.
Changing a generation expression changes only column data, not its type, so re-validating constraints is enough.
Re-validation avoids an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock on the whole partition hierarchy when only one partition changes.
Rebuilding dependents under alter table only contradicts the meaning of ONLY.
The fix is too complex for back branches, so they should get the error.
brief.thread_state: Alberto Piai is the only reviewer and withdrew his idea of also rebuilding the parent constraint. He prefers the re-validation approach for constraints and says that set expression with ONLY failing depending on dependencies would surprise users; v4 answers his points, and the CommitFest entry needs a rebase.
unclear: Which of the two v4 patches the author wants committed to master, and which to back branches.
Whether the new errors break existing scripts that run set expression with ONLY on a parent with indexes on the column.
The root cause of the "could not read blocks" error with an index and a foreign key; the author did not investigate it.
How the second patch handles plain inheritance children, as opposed to partitions.
Whether the documentation for alter table changes; the patches touch no documentation files.
How virtual generated columns behave differently, though their tests change too.

prior_attempts.title: Fix ALTER TABLE DROP EXPRESSION with ONLY option
prior_attempts.reason: The visible messages do not show why. Peter Eisentraut asked why tablecmds.c passes recurse = false when recursing, and suggested a more consistent use of the two flags would make the existing code work. Tom Lane said that if the flags matter here, DROP EXPRESSION should not use ATSimpleRecursion. The author replied in December 2025 that v3 is correct, and no later reply appears before the entry was returned with feedback.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P1 changed DROP EXPRESSION recursion checks for multi-level inheritance; this proposal fixes dependent-object handling for set expression on partitions and with ONLY.

objections.title: Back-branch fix makes working ALTER TABLE ONLY ... SET EXPRESSION fail
objections.failure_scenario: A migration script on 17.x runs alter table only t alter column b set expression on a partitioned parent that has an index on b and no foreign key. Today it succeeds. After a minor upgrade with the disallow patch it fails, and the user finds out when the deployment stops partway.
objections.argument: Message #2 says the ONLY case works when only an index depends on the column, yet v4 of the disallow patch rejects ONLY whenever any dependency exists (message #6). That turns a working command into an error in a stable release to fix a different, narrower failure. A committer would likely ask that a back-branch fix block only the cases that lose constraints or corrupt the rebuild, and leave working ones alone.
objections.author_must_show: Which ALTER TABLE ONLY ... SET EXPRESSION cases that succeed today would the back-branch patch reject, and why must those be rejected rather than left working?

precedents.title: ALTER TABLE - check for column existence before starting operations

critic.reasoning: Message #2 says the ONLY case works once the index is removed, yet the v4 disallow patch rejects ONLY with any dependency. The thread gives no stable-branch reason beyond the meaning of ONLY. P6 must not be used as support.

objections.title: SET EXPRESSION gets its own dependent-handling path apart from ALTER TYPE
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch changes how ATPostAlterTypeCleanup rebuilds constraints or adds a dependent kind. It updates the rebuild path and misses the new SET EXPRESSION re-validation path. No test fails, and a partition is left with a constraint that was never checked against the new data.
objections.argument: Message #6 says v4 moves changedConstraintOids into tab->constraints for SET EXPRESSION only and removes that logic from ATPostAlterTypeCleanup. Dependents are also collected in phase 1 and then reset to NIL. AT_PASS_ALTER_TYPE and AT_PASS_SET_EXPRESSION used to share one cleanup step, and v4 splits it. Message #6 also found v3 incorrect because of pass ordering, which shows how easy it is to get this split wrong.
objections.author_must_show: Can the re-validation rule live inside RememberConstraintForRebuilding and ATPostAlterTypeCleanup, as message #5 suggests, so one place decides rebuild or re-check for both commands?

critic.reasoning: Message #6 confirms v4 handles constraints for set expression apart from the shared ATPostAlterTypeCleanup logic. Message #5 asked for the rule to live in the Remember*ForRebuilding functions, and v4 does not say why it did not.

objections.title: No guidance for clusters that already lost inherited constraints
objections.failure_scenario: A PG17 user ran set expression on a partition, lost the inherited CHECK, then inserted rows that violate it. After the minor update the partition still has no pg_constraint row and no error appears. A later pg_dump restore re-inherits cc through partition of, and copy fails on the violating rows.
objections.argument: Message #1 shows the bug deletes pg_constraint rows for inherited CHECK and NOT NULL constraints. Both v4 patches only prevent new damage. Neither commit message says how to find affected partitions or repair them. For a back-branch fix that leaves bad catalog state behind, a committer would likely ask for a detection query and repair steps in the release notes before pushing.
objections.author_must_show: What query finds partitions whose inherited CHECK or NOT NULL constraint was dropped, and how should users repair them?

critic.reasoning: Message #1 shows the bug removes pg_constraint rows, and neither patch finds or repairs partitions that are already affected. The patch does not cause this damage, so this is a release-note request and does not block the design.

refuted.title: Back-branch error breaks ONLY set expression that works today
refuted.failure_scenario: A user's migration runs alter table only t alter column b set expression on a partitioned parent where b has only an index. That succeeds on 17.x today. After a minor upgrade with the bugfix patch, the same script fails with the new error during a deploy.
refuted.argument: Message #2 reports that ONLY with only an index dependency works, yet the patch disallows it so that ONLY keeps its meaning. That makes a working command fail in a minor release, which is the backward-compatibility concern recorded for an earlier ALTER TABLE check patch [P6]. Alberto Piai (message #5) said users would find this failure surprising, and message #6 keeps the error without answering him. The proposal needs a narrower back-branch error that targets only the broken cases.
refuted.author_must_show: Can the back-branch error be limited to the cases that drop constraints or fail today, leaving index-only ONLY cases working?

precedents.title: ALTER TABLE - check for column existence before starting operations

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. P6 concerned a new check on master and should not be used as support for a back-branch concern.

refuted.title: Success of SET EXPRESSION depends on which dependent object types exist
refuted.failure_scenario: A user changes a partition's generation expression on master and it succeeds while the column has only CHECK and NOT NULL constraints. A later create index on the parent, which cascades to every partition, makes the same command fail. On a back branch it fails in both cases, so one script behaves three ways.
refuted.argument: The POC accepts NOT NULL, CHECK and FOREIGN KEY dependents and still rejects index dependents (message #4). Any index on the column of a partitioned table creates partition indexes, so the error remains common. Message #5 says users would find dependency-driven failures surprising. The proposal does not say which patch goes to master, and no documentation hunk describes the error conditions for users.
refuted.author_must_show: What exact rule will the ALTER TABLE documentation give for when SET EXPRESSION on a partition or with ONLY is refused, on master and on back branches?

critic.reasoning: The v4 commit message says set expression on a partition whose index belongs to an index hierarchy already fails today, so the index case is not a new failure. The rest is documentation, which is out of scope, and the branch question in maintenance-fit-3.

refuted.title: Back-branch fix turns a working ALTER TABLE ONLY case into an error
refuted.failure_scenario: A user on 17 runs `alter table only t alter column b set expression as (...)` on a partitioned table that has an index on b and no foreign key. This works today. After a minor update the bugfix patch rejects it, and the deploy script fails at upgrade time.
refuted.argument: Message #2 says this case works when the column has only an index, then proposes to disallow it because rebuilding child indexes "could contradict the word ONLY". That is a semantic preference, and a stable branch is the wrong place to enforce it. The author did not investigate the root cause of the "could not read blocks" error, so the error may also hide a bug that ALTER TYPE shares. Message #5 objects to ONLY failing depending on dependencies, and message #6 keeps the error.
refuted.author_must_show: Can the back-branch error be limited to the cases that lose constraints or fail today, leaving the working index-only ONLY case alone?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1. The added point that ALTER TYPE may share the bug has no support in the thread.

refuted.title: Master and back branches would differ in SET EXPRESSION semantics
refuted.failure_scenario: A user tests `alter table part alter column b set expression` on master, where it succeeds with CHECK and FK dependents. The same script fails on 17 and 18 with the new error. Later fixes in this area of tablecmds.c need separate versions for each branch.
refuted.argument: Message #4 proposes errors for back branches and the proof of concept for master, and it is still open which one goes where. Two behaviours for one command across supported branches mean each later fix needs separate back-patch versions. Only one reviewer is engaged, and that reviewer says he is still learning the area (message #3). No committer who knows ATPostAlterTypeCleanup has replied.
refuted.author_must_show: Which v4 patch is meant for master and which for back branches, and has a committer familiar with ATPostAlterTypeCleanup agreed to carry the split?

critic.reasoning: Message #4 says back branches get the error, and the re-validation patch is a proof of concept for later work. An error on stable branches with a fuller fix on master is existing practice, and a missing committer is a committability point.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: see objection replication-ondisk-1: No guidance for clusters that already lost inherited constraints

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: The bug deletes inherited pg_constraint rows on partitions; the patches change when those rows are dropped or kept.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: The bugfix patch changes what alter table only ... set expression accepts, based on the meaning of ONLY.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: A partition that already lost an inherited CHECK gets it back on restore, which can fail on rows that violate it.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The bugfix patch targets stable branches and adds errors for commands that are accepted today.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The second patch gives set expression a constraint re-validation path in tablecmds.c apart from ATPostAlterTypeCleanup.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Which alter table only ... set expression cases that succeed today does the back-branch patch reject, and why must each be rejected?
What is the root cause of the "could not read blocks" error in message #2, and does the new error cover every case that reaches it?
Can the re-validation rule live in RememberConstraintForRebuilding and ATPostAlterTypeCleanup, so that one place decides between rebuild and re-check?
What query finds partitions whose inherited CHECK or NOT NULL constraint was already dropped, and how should users repair them?
How does the second patch handle plain inheritance children, as opposed to partitions?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows the ALTER TABLE phase 2 and phase 3 code in tablecmds.c, in particular ATPostAlterTypeCleanup and constraint inheritance on partitions. No committer has replied in the visible thread.
committability.liability: A behaviour change in stable branches from 17 on: any script that the new error breaks is reported against the minor release. On master, the owner also signs for a second constraint-handling path that later ALTER TABLE patches must keep correct.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted four patch versions, answered the reviewer's points in v4 and moved the entry to the next CommitFest. The entry needs a rebase since 2026-08-27.

priority.reason: Silent loss of inherited constraints is a correctness bug worth fixing, though only users who run set expression on a partition or with ONLY hit it. Both patches touch only tablecmds.c and tests, but the back-branch scope needs a decision from a committer, and none is engaged.

provisional_note: Without the code I could not check which dependency cases the new errors reject, or whether phase 3 re-validation covers every constraint kind for partitions, plain inheritance children and virtual generated columns. Only 3 of 6 messages were visible.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: generated columns
precedents_retrieved.summary: Peter Eisentraut proposed implementing SQL-standard generated columns (GENERATED ALWAYS AS (expr)), with the generation expression stored in pg_attrdef like a default and MySQL/Oracle-style VIRTUAL|STORED syntax. Only the VIRTUAL (computed-on-read) variant was fully implemented; STORED, various ALTER TABLE forms and index support were deferred.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Review by Jaime Casanova found multiple bugs: generated columns showed no value through a view, inheritance produced a malformed default and a server crash on insert, ALTER COLUMN TYPE on the referenced or generated column failed with internal errors, triggers saw NULL for the generated column, and the generation expression could be dropped via DROP DEFAULT. Based on these reviews, the commitfest manager marked the entry Returned with feedback, asking for an updated version to be resubmitted.

precedents_retrieved.title: ALTER TABLE - check for column existence before starting operations
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a check in the first (preparation) pass of ALTER TABLE so that a column referenced by a subcommand such as SET NOT NULL is verified to exist, or to be added by another subcommand, before any expensive work like building a primary key starts. The goal is to fail fast on typos instead of holding a long lock and generating WAL that is then discarded.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The only review raised a memory-release issue (the heap tuple not being freed) and a behavioural regression: because subcommands run in passes by type, a command that alters a column and adds the same column later in the list used to succeed and fails with the patch, which could break backward compatibility. The visible messages show no revised patch or author reply after that review, and the entry was returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Improving default column names/aliases of subscript text expressions
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch changes the default column name for a subscript expression with a string-literal subscript, such as data['a'] on jsonb, to the subscript value instead of the base column name. A later POC derives the name from the transformed expression and leaves room for type-specific hooks, so subscript implementations could supply their own default alias.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that changing default column names breaks existing queries, and that a GUC to switch the behavior would change query semantics. He was not convinced the new names were better, preferring names like "data_a" if anything changed. He called the transformed-expression POC a single-purpose kluge and suggested that extensible field selection would serve the author's use case better.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add support for ALTER INDEX .. ALTER [COLUMN] col_num {SET,RESET}
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add `alter index ... alter [column] col_num set/reset (...)` so opclass parameters on an index column can be changed after `create index`, using a column number as `set statistics` does. The patch stores the new values in pg_attribute attoptions, checks them with index_opclass_options(), and does not rebuild the index.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Changing an opclass parameter such as siglen without a rebuild leaves the index inconsistent with its options. Nathan Bossart reproduced test failures in hstore after `alter index hidx alter column 1 set (siglen=100)`, which went away after a REINDEX. Alexander Korotkov said the known uses for opclass options all need a rebuild and suggested keeping the options immutable until real cases for mutable ones appear. The author agreed the patch was not enough, and the entry was withdrawn.

precedents_retrieved.title: Change a constraint's index - ALTER TABLE ... ALTER CONSTRAINT ... USING INDEX ...
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Alvaro Herrera, Laurenz Albe
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds ALTER TABLE ... ALTER CONSTRAINT ... USING INDEX to replace the index behind an EXCLUDE, UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY or FOREIGN KEY constraint with a similar index. The main use case is swapping a primary key index for one with INCLUDE columns, or back.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane wanted the feature rejected because a primary key with a swapped index is no longer an accurate primary key, and information_schema cannot describe it. Alvaro Herrera and Laurenz Albe agreed that primary keys with INCLUDE columns would first need PRIMARY KEY syntax, so that pg_dump works. That leaves this command a narrow use case. The author did not answer the review, and Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent proposes the same fix. P19 is close in area but has no recorded reason, so it is not used.
The core bug, silent loss of inherited constraints, deserves a fix; the objections cover only the user-facing contract of the proposed errors.

Beyond the catalog cleanup point, neither patch changes on-disk format, WAL records, replication, wire protocol or extension API. The re-validation patch keeps constraint rows and their stored expressions, which stays valid because the column type does not change.

Both patches change how set expression handles constraints and indexes on a generated column; neither adds a privilege, role, view or protocol path. Ownership checks on the altered table stay as they are, and the bugfix narrows what a partition owner can do by stopping the silent drop of inherited CHECK and NOT NULL constraints. FK re-validation in the second patch uses the existing phase 3 RI path, so I see no new escalation, leak or unbounded resource use.
The bug is real, the fix has no hot-path cost, and it adds no new dependency. These objections are about the scope of the back-branch error and the long-run shape of the code.

The proposal fixes silent loss of inherited CHECK and NOT NULL constraints, plus a read error, inside core ALTER TABLE. No extension, setting or documented idiom gives correct behaviour here. The proof-of-concept patch reuses the existing phase 3 constraint validation and adds no second mechanism. Running SET EXPRESSION on the parent is not equivalent, because it changes every partition.

This is a bug fix: since PG17, set expression on a partition drops inherited CHECK and NOT NULL constraints without telling the user, and message #2 shows an internal read error. Silent loss of a constraint needs no demand evidence. Any user of generated columns on partitioned tables can hit it, and the costs fall only on that command.
